statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and the five slots up to the scheduled 22:00Z reopen contain no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the nineteen slots from the reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 9 and 15, every one of them far below the block threshold. Stress is 40, moderate: Friday's long-end pressure, Brent at 94.39 dollars after a second consecutive weekly gain above 5%, and a reported Monday US briefing on tightening economic pressure on Iran are all unpriced until the venue reopens. Confidence is 85, high, on index levels verified at the index owner plus H.15 yields, oil, volatility and a checked calendar, limited only by the absence of a live price path.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: the Nasdaq-100 opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day yet below its own open, while the VIX settled at 14.89 after a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced, so no persistent directional efficiency is on record. Tail-relevant structure cannot be observed again until the 22:00Z reopen, and the narrow evidence-based danger window therefore covers 22:00Z to 02:00Z, when the weekend information set is repriced into thin liquidity. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with nineteen reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through five shut hours, then carries conditional readings between 9 and 15 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen through a Monday US cash open that now sits deeper inside the window, while a partly reversed Treasury buyback rally, Brent above 94 dollars and a reported Monday US briefing on isolating Iran's economy stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T17:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T16:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the eighteen hours after it sit inside the horizon while the first five do not, and the Monday US cash open at 13:30Z plus the three following cash hours fall inside the window. The Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, having opened at 29,359.60 and traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range; this level is confirmed at the index owner, whose page carries the same high, low and net change. Both extremes were retraced and the index finished below its own open, which is mean-reverting rather than one-way behaviour. The broader tape agreed on the day: S&P 500 +0.43% at 7,674.37, Nasdaq Composite +0.43% at 26,180.46, Dow +0.98% at 53,277.01, yet the Nasdaq Composite lost 2.0% on the week and the S&P 500 1.4%, so the weekly trend and the daily print disagree. Volatility compressed into the close, with the VIX at 14.89, down 6.0%, after a 14.77-15.95 range, which is not the configuration from which no-retracement trends usually start. The pressure sits in fixed income and commodities rather than in equity volatility: the latest H.15 constant maturity series shows the 2-year at 4.19%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, and Friday's session reporting put the 10-year near 4.73% and the 30-year near 5.27% after an expanded Treasury buyback programme was read as a limited fix and yields snapped back. Brent at 94.39 dollars and WTI at 87.06 dollars have now risen more than 5% in each of the last two weeks with Strait of Hormuz transits reported near a fifth of the pre-war average. The shared delayed cross-asset context for the latest session is consistent with this reading and adds nothing that would change it: index futures modestly higher, the volatility future lower, gold sharply higher, Treasury futures lower across the curve, five of eight megacaps positive but the semiconductor group softer on average into Nvidia week. None of that is live Nasdaq-100 price-path evidence and it is not treated as such. Because no venue is open, Tail cannot be scored on structure and holds its closed-venue floor of 4 for the current hour and the four shut hours after it. From the 22:00Z reopen the forecast carries conditional Tail between 9 and 15, peaking at 13 in the first full hour after the reopen and at 15 in the first full US cash hour on Monday, both comfortably below the 25 threshold. Stress of 40 is the honest reading of an unpriced weekend set rather than of any observed distress, and it rises to 49 across the reopen before decaying through the Asian hours. Confidence of 85 reflects verified index, yield, oil, volatility and calendar evidence, discounted only for the missing live price path. The week ahead concentrates its risk on Wednesday and Friday, with July PCE, the second GDP estimate and durable goods at 12:30Z on Wednesday, Nvidia's results after that session's close, and the new Fed Chair's first Jackson Hole keynote at 14:00Z on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available, while the 21:00Z clock-hour on 22 August and the 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z clock-hours on 23 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress decayed steadily across the shut weekend from 41 at the start of the window to a low of 34 in the European morning, then turned higher through the afternoon and reached 39 in the most recent published hour as the reopen drew closer. Confidence eased from 87 to 85 as the last observed session receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The next four slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress climbs from 40 to 45 as the reopen approaches with the weekend information set unpriced. The final nineteen slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12 and the first full hour after it 13, on the untested assumption that a weekend gap could extend before retracing. Conditional Tail then decays to 9 through the quiet Asian hours, where two-way trade has historically been most reliable, before rebuilding through the European session to 12 into the 12:30Z Chicago Fed release, 14 at the 13:30Z US cash open and a horizon peak of 15 in the first full cash hour, still ten points below the block threshold. Stress follows a similar shape, peaking at 49 across the reopen and at 48 in the first full cash hour, and Confidence decays from 85 to 71 with distance from the verified Friday levels. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the danger window is deliberately narrow at 22:00Z to 02:00Z, covering only the thin-liquidity repricing of the weekend set rather than the whole session.
